issues.title: 🐔 Animals that unlock with contribution streaks
issues.body:
## Idea
Reward streaks with farm animals that wander around the field:

| Streak | Unlocks |
| --- | --- |
| 7 days | 🐔 Chicken |
| 30 days | 🐄 Cow |
| 100 days | 🐕 Dog that follows the farmer |

The longest streak of the year decides which animals live on the farm.

## Where to start
- Compute the longest streak from `weeks` (same data the renderer already receives).
- Add sprites to `src/sprites.js` (8×8 or 12×12, same palette system).
- Animate them in `src/render.js` with CSS keyframes only (no JS: GitHub strips scripts from SVGs). A simple back-and-forth walk along the fence is enough for a first version.

## Done when
- [ ] Streak calculation with a small test
- [ ] At least the chicken sprite + idle/walk animation
- [ ] Animals appear only if the streak threshold is met
- [ ] README table updated

issues.title: 🎃 Scarecrow on your best day
issues.body:
## Idea
Place a scarecrow on the plot of the day with the most contributions, with a tiny sign like `best day: 23`.

## Where to start
- Find the max `count` in `weeks`.
- Draw a scarecrow sprite in `src/sprites.js`.
- In `src/render.js`, render it on top of that plot once the farmer has passed it (reuse the `on(t)` keyframe helper).

## Done when
- [ ] Scarecrow appears on the correct day
- [ ] Small label with the count
- [ ] Looks good with the 5 existing crops

issues.title: 🏠 Barn that grows with your yearly contributions
issues.body:
## Idea
A building next to the field that upgrades with your total contributions in the last year:

- < 100 → small shack
- 100–999 → red barn
- 1000+ → barn with silo

## Where to start
- The total is already passed to `renderFarm` as `total`.
- The header area or the right margin of the field has room for it; the SVG width can grow a bit if needed.

## Done when
- [ ] 3 sprites (one per tier)
- [ ] Tier chosen from `total`
- [ ] Layout still fits GitHub's README width

issues.title: 📋 Stats on the wooden sign: longest streak and best day
issues.body:
## Idea
The sign currently shows the username, total contributions and crop. Add a second line of stats, for example:

`🔥 longest streak: 12 days · ⭐ best day: Mar 14 (23)`

## Where to start
- `src/render.js`, look for `subtitle`.
- Keep the sign width calculation (`signW`) in sync so text doesn't overflow.

## Done when
- [ ] Longest streak and best day computed from `weeks`
- [ ] Sign grows to fit, no overlap with the legend

issues.title: 🧺 Harvest counter at the end of the loop
issues.body:
## Idea
When the farmer finishes walking the field, show a counter that ticks up like in farming games: `+799 🌻`.

## Where to start
- Timeline constants live at the top of `src/render.js` (`EXIT`, `HOLD`, `FADE`).
- CSS can't animate text content, so a counter can be faked with stacked `<text>` elements that appear one after another, or with a single pop-in + scale animation.

## Done when
- [ ] Counter appears during the HOLD phase
- [ ] Fades out with the rest of the field

issues.title: 🚿 Farmer waters the plants on harvest days
issues.body:
## Idea
When the farmer reaches a level-4 day, he pauses for a moment with a watering can and a few droplets fall.

## Where to start
- Farmer movement keyframes are built in `src/render.js` (`moves`). A pause means adding an extra keyframe at the same position and shifting the timeline.
- New sprites: watering can frame for the farmer, 2–3 droplet pixels.

## Done when
- [ ] Watering frame + droplets
- [ ] Timeline still loops cleanly

issues.title: 🍂 Seasons (including tropical rainy/dry seasons)
issues.body:
## Idea
The farm changes with the date it was generated:

- Temperate: spring flowers, summer, autumn leaves, winter snow
- Tropical: rainy season (puddles, greener grass) and dry season (yellowish grass)

New input: `season: auto | spring | summer | autumn | winter | rainy | dry | none`.

## Where to start
- Ground colors are in `PALETTE` (`src/sprites.js`); seasons could be palette overrides.
- `auto` needs a hemisphere or climate hint. Maybe `auto` = temperate north by default, and users pick the rest.

## Done when
- [ ] At least 2 seasons implemented
- [ ] `season` input in `action.yml` and CLI flag
- [ ] Docs in README

issues.title: 🌙 Day/night cycle based on when you usually code
issues.body:
## Idea
Night owls get a night farm (dark sky, moon, fireflies); early birds get a sunrise.

## Open question
The contribution calendar doesn't include times. Options:
- GraphQL `commitContributionsByRepository` → commit timestamps (needs more API calls)
- Public events API (only ~90 days)

Discussion welcome before implementing!

## Done when
- [ ] Approach agreed in this issue
- [ ] Night palette + fireflies animation
- [ ] Graceful fallback to day when data is missing

issues.title: ☁️ Passing weather: cloud shadows and light rain
issues.body:
## Idea
Soft cloud shadows drifting across the field, and occasionally a short light rain.

## Where to start
- Pure CSS: a semi-transparent dark shape with a long `translateX` animation over the field group in `src/render.js`.
- Rain: a few 1×3 px rects falling with staggered delays.

## Done when
- [ ] Cloud shadows look subtle (shouldn't hide the crops)
- [ ] Optional `weather: true|false` input

issues.title: 🧑‍🌾 Customizable farmer colors
issues.body:
## Idea
Let people dress their farmer:

```yaml
farmer_hat: "#efc96d"
farmer_shirt: "#d9473b"
farmer_overalls: "#3d72bd"
```

Stretch goal: pick the colors automatically from the dominant colors of the user's GitHub avatar.

## Where to start
- Farmer colors are the `H/h`, `P/p`, `U/u` entries in `PALETTE` (`src/sprites.js`). `spriteRects` already accepts a custom palette.

## Done when
- [ ] Inputs in `action.yml` + CLI flags
- [ ] Colors validated (hex)
- [ ] README example

issues.title: 🌽🍅 Mixed crops from your top languages
issues.body:
## Idea
If you use several languages, plant several crops in proportion: 60% Python → corn, 40% TypeScript → sunflowers.

## Where to start
- `fetchTopLanguage` in `src/github.js` already builds a tally; return the top 3 with shares.
- In `src/render.js`, choose the crop per plot deterministically (e.g. with the existing `hash()` helper) so the farm doesn't change on every run.

## Done when
- [ ] Up to 3 crops mixed by share
- [ ] `crop` input still forces a single crop
- [ ] Sign shows the mix

issues.title: 🌐 Web generator: type a username, see the farm
issues.body:
## Idea
A small site where anyone types their username and instantly sees their farm, plus an embeddable URL:

```md
![farm](https://gitfarm.vercel.app/api/farm?user=octocat)
```

This removes the "set up a workflow" step and is what makes tools like github-readme-stats spread.

## Where to start
- `generate()` in `src/generate.js` already does everything; it needs a serverless wrapper (Vercel/Netlify) that returns the SVG.
- Needs a server-side token and caching (`Cache-Control`) to stay within API limits.

## Done when
- [ ] `/api/farm?user=&crop=` endpoint
- [ ] Landing page with input + preview + copy-paste snippet
- [ ] Caching

issues.title: 🎞️ Export the farm as GIF/MP4 for sharing
issues.body:
## Idea
A `--gif` / `--mp4` option that records the animation, so people can share their farm on social media where SVGs don't play.

## Where to start
- Render frames with a headless browser (Playwright/Puppeteer) by pausing `document.getAnimations()` at each timestamp, then stitch with ffmpeg.
- Keep it as an optional dev dependency so the Action stays dependency-free.

## Done when
- [ ] Script that outputs a looping GIF/MP4
- [ ] Documented in README

issues.title: 🌱 Add your crop! (sprite contribution guide)
issues.body:
## Idea
Crops are the easiest way to contribute: no deep JS needed, just pixel art.

Each crop is two 8×8 grids in `src/sprites.js` (`grown` and `harvest`), where each character is a palette color and `.` is transparent:

```js
harvest: [
  "..w.w...",
  "...wL...",
  ".lLDYy..",
  // ...
],
```

## To add a crop
1. Add `grown` and `harvest` sprites to `CROPS` in `src/sprites.js` (add palette colors if needed).
2. Map languages to it in `src/crops.js` and add it to `CROP_NAMES`.
3. Run `node src/cli.js --demo --crop yourcrop --out demo.svg` and attach a screenshot to your PR.

## Wanted crops
- [ ] 🍓 Strawberry
- [ ] 🎃 Pumpkin
- [ ] 🍫 Cacao
- [ ] 🥕 Carrot
- [ ] 🍚 Rice

Comment which one you're taking so nobody duplicates work!

issues.title: 🧪 Tests for the calendar parser and renderer
issues.body:
## Idea
Add tests with the built-in `node:test` runner (no dependencies):

- Scraper: parse a saved snippet of GitHub's contributions HTML (`src/github.js` → `scrapeCalendar`).
- Levels: `withLevels` in `src/demo.js` maps counts to 0–4 correctly.
- Renderer: `renderFarm` returns a valid SVG with one plot per day and the expected keyframes.

## Done when
- [ ] `npm test` runs `node --test`
- [ ] A GitHub workflow runs tests on PRs
